concepts.title: Equality in Indian Democracy
concepts.description: Equality in Indian Democracy — part of the chapter on On Equality.
key_ideas: Core principles of equality in indian democracy
Step-by-step problem solving for equality in indian democracy
Real-world applications of equality in indian democracy

concepts.title: Equal Right to Vote
concepts.description: Introduction to the concept of political equality through the voting process, establishing that every adult citizen has equal power in a democracy regardless of their background.
key_ideas: Definition of Universal Adult Franchise
Voting rights for all citizens aged 18 and above
The idea of 'one person, one vote'
Contrast between political equality and economic inequality

concepts.title: Recognizing Dignity
concepts.description: Exploration of social inequalities based on caste, religion, and gender, and how unequal treatment violates a person's self-respect and dignity.
key_ideas: Understanding the term 'dignity' as self-respect
Impact of caste-based discrimination (Case study: Omprakash Valmiki)
Impact of religious discrimination (Case study: The Ansaris)
The relationship between equality and self-worth

concepts.title: Implementing Equality: Laws and Schemes
concepts.description: Examination of the two main ways the government tries to achieve equality: through constitutional laws and through specific welfare programs.
key_ideas: Enforcing equality through the Constitution
Government schemes to help disadvantaged communities
Case Study: The Mid-day Meal Scheme
Benefits of schemes: Increased attendance and social socialization

concepts.title: Issues of Equality in Other Democracies
concepts.description: A comparative look at struggles for equality outside India, specifically focusing on the Civil Rights Movement in the United States.
key_ideas: Inequality is a global phenomenon in democracies
The African-American struggle for equal rights
The story of Rosa Parks
The Civil Rights Act of 1964

chapters.title: Role of the Government in Health

concepts.title: Public Health Services
concepts.description: Public Health Services — part of the chapter on Role of the Government in Health.
key_ideas: Core principles of public health services
Step-by-step problem solving for public health services
Real-world applications of public health services

concepts.title: Meaning of Health
concepts.description: Explores the definition of health beyond just the absence of disease, including factors like clean drinking water, sanitation, nutrition, and stress-free living.
key_ideas: Health is more than just being free from illness
Impact of clean water and pollution-free environment
Relationship between mental strain and physical health

concepts.title: Private Health Facilities
concepts.description: Examines healthcare services owned by individuals or companies for profit, contrasting them with public services in terms of cost, availability, and urban concentration.
key_ideas: Private facilities are not owned or controlled by the government
Patients pay high costs for services and medicines
Concentration of private doctors and hospitals in urban areas

concepts.title: Healthcare and Equality
concepts.description: Investigates whether adequate healthcare is available to all citizens, focusing on the disparity between the high cost of private care and the overcrowding of public centers.
key_ideas: The rising cost of private treatments creates financial hardship
Barriers to access for the poor, women, and tribal communities
The government's constitutional duty to ensure welfare and right to life

concepts.title: The Kerala Experience
concepts.description: A case study on how the state of Kerala improved health standards by decentralizing the budget and empowering local Panchayats to manage water, food, and education.
key_ideas: Decentralization of funds (40% given to Panchayats)
Focus on basic needs: water, food, and women's development
Success of village-level planning in improving health outcomes

concepts.title: The Costa Rican Approach
concepts.description: Analyzes the policy decision of Costa Rica to not have an army and instead divert those funds toward public health, sanitation, and education.
key_ideas: Decision to disband the army to save funds
Prioritizing health education at all levels
Government provision of safe drinking water and housing

concepts.title: Legislature and Executive
concepts.description: Legislature and Executive — part of the chapter on How the State Government Works.
key_ideas: Core principles of legislature and executive
Step-by-step problem solving for legislature and executive
Real-world applications of legislature and executive

concepts.title: MLAs and Constituencies
concepts.description: Introduction to how states are divided into electoral areas and how representatives are elected by the people.
key_ideas: Definition of a Constituency
Election of Members of Legislative Assembly (MLAs)
Direct election by the people
One representative per constituency

concepts.title: Ruling Party and Opposition
concepts.description: Explains how a government is formed based on election results, the concept of a majority, and the role of those not in power.
key_ideas: Criteria for a majority (more than half the seats)
Formation of the Ruling Party
Role and function of the Opposition
Coalition governments when no single party wins

concepts.title: The Role of the Governor
concepts.description: Distinguishes between the Head of the State and the Head of the Government, focusing on the Governor's constitutional duties.
key_ideas: Governor as the Head of the State
Appointment by the Central Government
Duty to ensure the state runs by the Constitution
Appointing the Chief Minister and other ministers

concepts.title: Debates in the Legislative Assembly
concepts.description: Examines how the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) functions as a place for debate, questioning, and discussing current issues.
key_ideas: MLAs asking questions to ministers
Debating problems and suggesting solutions
Ministers responding and assuring action
The common responsibility of all MLAs

concepts.title: Media and Government Accountability
concepts.description: Explores how the government communicates its work to the public outside the assembly and how it is held accountable.
key_ideas: Role of press conferences
Newspapers and media as watchdogs
Government response to public protests
Transparency in government functioning

chapters.title: Growing Up as Boys and Girls

concepts.title: Gender Roles and Stereotypes
concepts.description: Gender Roles and Stereotypes — part of the chapter on Growing Up as Boys and Girls.
key_ideas: Core principles of gender roles and stereotypes
Step-by-step problem solving for gender roles and stereotypes
Real-world applications of gender roles and stereotypes

concepts.title: Gender Socialization
concepts.description: Explores how society teaches children specific behaviors, values, and responsibilities based on their biological sex, often using toys, games, and school environments as tools.
key_ideas: Distinction between growing up in different cultural contexts (e.g., Samoa vs. Madhya Pradesh)
Toys and games as tools for teaching future gender roles
Different behavioral expectations for boys and girls in public spaces

concepts.title: Valuing Housework
concepts.description: Examines the societal tendency to devalue domestic labor because it is usually unpaid and associated with women, challenging the notion that housework is 'natural' rather than learned work.
key_ideas: Housework is often not recognized as 'real work' because it is unpaid
The assumption that caregiving is a natural duty of women
The impact of devaluing housework on women's status in society

concepts.title: Invisible and Physically Demanding Labor
concepts.description: Breaks down domestic chores into specific tasks to highlight that they are physically strenuous, time-consuming, and often invisible to other family members.
key_ideas: Domestic work involves heavy physical tasks (fetching water, carrying firewood, washing)
Housework is time-consuming, leaving little time for leisure
The concept of 'invisible' work that is only noticed when it is not done

concepts.title: The Double Burden
concepts.description: Discusses the situation where women participate in the paid workforce outside the home while still retaining the primary responsibility for unpaid domestic chores.
key_ideas: Definition of double burden (working inside and outside the home)
Impact on women's health and time
Comparison of total work hours between men and women

concepts.title: Government Role and Support Systems
concepts.description: Identifies constitutional provisions for equality and specific government initiatives designed to support working women and reduce the burden of childcare.
key_ideas: Constitutional mandate against gender discrimination
Role of Anganwadis (child care centers) in villages
Laws requiring creche facilities in organizations with female employees

concepts.title: Media and Its Role in Democracy
concepts.description: Media and Its Role in Democracy — part of the chapter on Understanding Media.
key_ideas: Core principles of media and its role in democracy
Step-by-step problem solving for media and its role in democracy
Real-world applications of media and its role in democracy

concepts.title: Forms of Media and Changing Technology
concepts.description: Explores the definition of media, the distinction between print and electronic media, and how evolving technology improves the quality and reach of mass media.
key_ideas: Definition of 'Media' as the plural of 'Medium'
Difference between Print Media (newspapers) and Electronic Media (TV, radio)
How technology affects sound, image quality, and public reach

concepts.title: Media and Money
concepts.description: Examines the financial structure of mass media, focusing on the high costs of technology and the reliance on advertising revenue.
key_ideas: High cost of equipment (cameras, satellites, sound recorders)
Role of big business houses in owning media outlets
Advertisements as the primary source of revenue

concepts.title: Balanced Reporting and Independence
concepts.description: Discusses the importance of independent journalism and the factors that prevent media from providing a balanced view, such as business interests.
key_ideas: Definition of a balanced report (discussing all points of view)
The concept of Independent Media
Influence of corporate control on news bias

concepts.title: Setting the Agenda
concepts.description: Analyzes how the media decides which stories to focus on, thereby shaping public perception and deciding what is considered 'newsworthy'.
key_ideas: Media's power to shape public thoughts and feelings
Examples of agenda setting (e.g., highlighting environmental issues vs. fashion weeks)
The responsibility of media to focus on significant social issues

concepts.title: Censorship and Regulations
concepts.description: Explains the government's power to disallow certain media content from being published or shown to the public.
key_ideas: Definition of Censorship
Government certification of films (Censor Board)
Historical context of censorship (e.g., The Emergency of 1975-1977)

concepts.title: Weekly Markets and Shopping Complexes
concepts.description: Weekly Markets and Shopping Complexes — part of the chapter on Markets Around Us.
key_ideas: Core principles of weekly markets and shopping complexes
Step-by-step problem solving for weekly markets and shopping complexes
Real-world applications of weekly markets and shopping complexes

concepts.title: Shops in the Neighborhood
concepts.description: Exploration of permanent shops located near residential areas that provide essential goods and services, often operating on trust and credit.
key_ideas: Proximity and convenience for consumers
Difference between permanent shops and roadside hawkers
The system of purchasing on credit (udhaar) based on trust

concepts.title: The Chain of Markets
concepts.description: Analysis of the series of exchanges that goods pass through, connecting the initial producer to the final consumer.
key_ideas: Linkage between producers and consumers
Goods traveling through multiple hands before reaching the shelf
Understanding that consumers rarely buy directly from factories or farms

concepts.title: Wholesale Markets and Traders
concepts.description: Detailed look at the role of the wholesaler who buys in large quantities directly from producers to sell to other traders.
key_ideas: Definition of wholesale vs. retail
Bulk purchasing and storage
The role of large wholesale markets (mandis) in cities

concepts.title: Markets Everywhere: Digital and Invisible
concepts.description: Examination of modern trading methods where buying and selling occur without visiting a physical shop, including online commerce and business-to-business transactions.
key_ideas: Ordering goods via phone or internet
Use of credit cards and digital payments
Invisible markets (e.g., medical representatives selling to doctors, farmers buying fertilizers)

concepts.title: Markets and Equality
concepts.description: Critical evaluation of the economic disparities between small traders (like hawkers) and large shop owners in shopping complexes.
key_ideas: Comparison of profit margins between small and big traders
Disparities in bargaining power
Impact of economic status on who can be a buyer or a seller
